title: Pulmonary tuberculosis (TB of the lungs)

items: Pulmonary tuberculosis is an infection of the lungs caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
It spreads through the air when someone with lung TB coughs.
A cough lasting more than 2 weeks, often with sputum that changes from dry to purulent.
Fever, night sweats, weight loss, and poor appetite.
Coughing up blood in some people.
Sputum smear for acid-fast bacilli (AFB), at least 2 samples.
A rapid molecular test such as Xpert MTB/RIF.
Sputum culture, which is the most sensitive test.
Chest X-ray and an HIV test.
TB is treated with a long course of several medicines, given under the care of your team.
Taking every dose is very important. Do not stop treatment without speaking to your team.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Cover your mouth when coughing, and wear a mask as advised.
Keep close contacts informed so they can be checked.
Sputum tests are repeated during treatment to check progress.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Coughing up large amounts of blood
Fever with confusion or feeling faint
